title: A path of contacts across time has a light cone, and on affine substrates every verdict is two row sequences per contact
subject: Paths of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: In a path of rings joined by shared contacts, the last contact cannot depend on the first ring before the lag one past the summed distances between the contacts of each middle ring, so the ends are bound only from then. For linear or affine rules and affine laws, a contact binds two rings at lag T exactly when its row of M^T meets both, so iterating rows until they repeat decides every verdict.
